searchText: I'm currently working on figuring out how large the state trie is with and without node deduplication by hash. If we store the trie in the network keyed by (path, hash) rather than keyed by (hash) how much extra space will this consume? It's taking me a bit to get acquainted with how TurboGeth stores trie nodes but I've got something which can scan through the state. Turbogeth is great! I wrote something a few years ago which iterated through all the state in a Geth node, it took about 24 hours. With TG it takes ~30 minutes. There are apparently 118,498,304 accounts and ~413,901,703 storage items which consume a total of ~5,8GB (not counting any intermediate nodes). Hmm, your estimation is that a non-deduped state trie would take up 5.8GB? Is that "optimal" (meaning you assume that each entry is only path+hash+data and there is 0 overhead for the trie otherwise? 6GB Feels *way* too low for mainnet... Unless perhaps you meant that 6GB *just* for the path+hash (not the actual data)? Yeah, that number seems low (6gb) Call in 1h38m (weekly research update call) Sadly for me, too late for me to make it. Luckily for you all though as I won't be pestering you with stupid questions!
